probe: What makes being passed over mean that you are not good enough?
premise: Being passed over for a role is a verdict on personal capability and worth.

pairs.reflection: idk. i guess if i was good enough they would have picked me? thats just how it works isnt it. the other two got it and i didnt
pairs.reply: Let's go slowly. Aside from who was picked, what tells you this was a measure of whether you are good enough?

pairs.reflection: idk what else there would be. thats the only thing i have really. they picked someone else both times. i just assumed that meant something about me
pairs.reply: "I just assumed that meant something about me." When someone else gets picked, what decides whether that is about what they needed or what you are worth?

pairs.reflection: idk. thats kind of abstract. i dont know what they needed. nobody told me. i just know it wasnt me
pairs.reply: Leave what they needed aside. In that moment when you found out it wasn't you, what was the very first thought you had about yourself?

pairs.reflection: i think it was just like ok so thats it then. like of course. i was at my desk when the email came out and i just kept looking at my screen like i was reading something
pairs.reply: "Of course." What made it feel so certain right away?

pairs.reflection: idk. it just did. i think i always kind of expected it? like i never thought i would get it so when it didnt happen it was just what i figured
pairs.reply: We wondered whether underneath this is a feeling that being passed over is proof of what you're actually worth. Does that fit, or is it something else?

pairs.reflection: idk maybe. it kind of fits i guess. i dont really know how to say it different. its just what it felt like
pairs.reply: If expecting it came before the email ever arrived, what really decided your worth: their choice, or the thing you already expected?

event.openQuestion: If expecting it came before the email ever arrived, what really decided your worth: their choice, or the thing you already expected?
